meta.source: Luminari MO Three-Layer Registry v1.0 — Northwest Hope Foundation

steps.action: Document the violation with timestamps. Photograph the issue. Keep all correspondence with landlord in writing (text or email). Note dates, times, conditions.
steps.documents_needed: Photos, written communications, lease copy
steps.deadline: 24 hours of discovering violation
steps.statute: RSMo §441.234 (MO URLTA — Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act)
steps.notes: Creates paper trail for all subsequent steps. MO URLTA applies to most residential rentals.

steps.action: Send written notice to landlord stating the violation, citing RSMo §441.234. Give landlord 14 days to remedy for non-emergency repairs, or reasonable time for emergency conditions.
steps.documents_needed: Written notice to landlord (certified mail recommended)
steps.deadline: Immediately after documenting — creates paper trail
steps.notes: 14-day notice required before rent withholding or repair-and-deduct under MO law

steps.action: File complaint with local code enforcement. In Kansas City: KC 311 or Neighborhood Services. In St. Louis: Building Division. Rural areas: contact county health department.
steps.documents_needed: Photos, correspondence, lease
steps.state_agency: KC 311 / STL Building Division / County Health Department
steps.deadline: Within days of violation
steps.notes: Code enforcement is local in MO — no statewide housing agency. KC and STL have strongest enforcement.

steps.action: Contact legal aid for tenant representation. LAWMO (western MO) or LSEM (eastern MO). Missouri Tenant Help (HUD-funded eviction defense statewide).
steps.documents_needed: All documentation, lease, correspondence, code enforcement reports
steps.deadline: Before any court hearing — immediately if eviction filed
steps.notes: Missouri Tenant Help is HUD-funded eviction defense for low-income renters statewide

steps.action: File housing discrimination complaint with MCHR (Missouri Commission on Human Rights) or HUD Kansas City Regional Office if discrimination is involved.
steps.documents_needed: Evidence of discriminatory conduct, timeline, correspondence
steps.deadline: 180 days from discriminatory act (MCHR) — SHORTER than federal 365 days
steps.notes: MCHR has SHORTER filing deadline than federal HUD (180 vs 365 days). Dual-file recommended.

steps.action: Escalate to Missouri AG Consumer Protection if pattern of landlord violations affecting multiple tenants. File complaint online.
steps.documents_needed: All prior documentation, evidence of pattern across tenants
steps.deadline: No strict deadline — pattern threshold: 3+ tenants with similar violations
steps.notes: AG can pursue injunctive relief and civil penalties for pattern violations

steps.action: Document all hours worked, pay received, and discrepancies. Save pay stubs, time records, texts/emails about hours or pay. Calculate amount owed.
steps.documents_needed: Pay stubs, time records, employment agreement, written communications
steps.deadline: Immediately — begin documentation
steps.notes: MO wage enforcement is weaker than most states — dual-file with federal DOL WHD recommended

steps.action: File wage complaint with Missouri Division of Labor Standards (DLS) — Wage and Hour Section. File online or by mail.
steps.documents_needed: Pay stubs, time records, employment agreement
steps.state_agency: MO Division of Labor Standards — Wage & Hour
steps.deadline: Within 2 years of wage violation (RSMo §290.527)
steps.notes: NOTE: MO enforcement weaker than most states — also file federal WHD complaint

steps.action: Simultaneously file with federal DOL Wage and Hour Division (WHD) — Kansas City area office. Federal FLSA enforcement is often more effective than MO state process.
steps.documents_needed: Same documentation as state filing
steps.state_agency: DOL Wage and Hour Division — Kansas City
steps.deadline: 2-year SOL (3 years if willful violation)
steps.statute: 29 USC §201 et seq. (Fair Labor Standards Act)
steps.notes: Federal WHD is often more effective than MO DLS for wage recovery — dual-file recommended

steps.action: File employment discrimination complaint with MCHR if wage theft involves discriminatory treatment. Also file with EEOC St. Louis District Office.
steps.documents_needed: Evidence of discriminatory pay practices, comparator information
steps.deadline: 180 days (MCHR) / 300 days (EEOC) — MCHR deadline SHORTER
steps.statute: Missouri Human Rights Act (RSMo Chapter 213), Title VII
steps.notes: MCHR and EEOC are FEPA dual-file partners — filing with one counts for both

steps.action: Contact legal aid for representation. LAWMO (western MO) or LSEM (eastern MO) handle wage theft cases for income-eligible workers.
steps.documents_needed: All prior documentation and filings
steps.deadline: Before SOL expires
steps.notes: Legal aid can pursue private action for unpaid wages + penalties

steps.action: Escalate to MO AG Consumer Protection if pattern of wage theft by same employer affecting 3+ workers.
steps.documents_needed: Evidence of pattern across multiple workers
steps.deadline: No strict deadline — pattern threshold: 3+ workers with same employer
steps.notes: AG can pursue pattern violations as unfair business practices

steps.action: Request written Notice of Action (NOA) from MO FSD. Document the denial reason, date received, and all communications with FSD caseworker.
steps.documents_needed: Notice of Action (NOA), application documents, income verification
steps.deadline: Request NOA immediately upon denial
steps.notes: NOA must state reason for denial and appeal rights — if not received, request in writing

steps.action: Request Administrative Fair Hearing within 90 days of NOA. Contact local FSD office or call 573-751-2730 (DSS Administrative Hearing Unit).
steps.documents_needed: NOA, supporting documents, income records
steps.deadline: 90 days from NOA — benefits may continue during appeal if requested within 10 days of NOA
steps.notes: CRITICAL: Request hearing within 10 days of NOA to continue benefits during appeal

steps.action: For unemployment denial: appeal to MO Division of Employment Security (DES) within 30 days of determination. File online at uinteract.labor.mo.gov.
steps.documents_needed: Determination letter, employment records, separation documentation
steps.state_agency: MO Division of Employment Security — Appeals
steps.deadline: 30 days from determination — SHORTER than many states
steps.notes: MO UI appeal deadline is 30 days — shorter than many states. Do not miss.

steps.action: Contact legal aid for representation at hearing. LAWMO (western MO), LSEM (eastern MO), MO Protection & Advocacy (disability benefits).
steps.documents_needed: All prior documentation, NOA, appeal filing
steps.deadline: Before hearing date
steps.notes: MO P&A specializes in SSI/SSDI and disability benefits appeals

steps.action: Escalate to MO Governor's Constituent Services or state legislators if DSS or DES is non-responsive for 60+ days.
steps.documents_needed: Timeline of all contacts, appeal filings, lack of response
steps.state_agency: MO Governor's Constituent Services / MO General Assembly
steps.deadline: After 60+ days of non-response from agency
steps.notes: Legislative oversight especially effective during session (Jan–May). Contact both state senator and representative.

steps.action: For MO HealthNet (Medicaid) systemic issues: escalate to HHS/CMS (federal Medicaid oversight) if state agency is systematically denying eligible applicants.
steps.documents_needed: Evidence of systematic denial pattern, individual case documentation
steps.deadline: No strict deadline — federal jurisdiction over federal Medicaid dollars
steps.notes: Federal jurisdiction over MO HealthNet federal funding — for systemic violations only

steps.action: Request written denial with specific reason codes and policy provisions cited. Document all communications with insurer. Request complete claim file.
steps.documents_needed: Denial letter, policy, claim file, medical records if health insurance
steps.deadline: Immediately upon denial
steps.notes: Insurer must provide written denial with specific reasons under MO law

steps.action: File internal appeal with insurance company. For health insurance: request independent medical review if denial is based on medical necessity.
steps.documents_needed: Denial letter, supporting medical records, policy provisions
steps.deadline: Within 180 days of denial (check policy for specific deadline)
steps.notes: Internal appeal is required before external review for most health insurance claims

steps.action: File complaint with Missouri Department of Insurance (MDI). MDI investigates unfair claim practices and can order corrective action.
steps.documents_needed: Denial letter, internal appeal result, policy, all correspondence
steps.deadline: No strict deadline — file promptly after internal appeal exhausted
steps.notes: MDI is Missouri's primary insurance regulator — can investigate and fine insurers

steps.action: For health insurance: request external review through MDI. Missouri has independent external review for health insurance medical necessity denials.
steps.documents_needed: Internal appeal denial, medical records, treating physician statement
steps.deadline: Within 4 months of internal appeal denial (RSMo §376.694)
steps.statute: RSMo §376.694 (Health Insurance External Review Act), §354.535 (HMO External Review)
steps.notes: External review decision is binding on insurer. Separate process for HMO plans under §354.535.

steps.action: Contact CLAIM (Missouri SHIP) for Medicare-related insurance issues. For MO HealthNet managed care: contact MO HealthNet Division.
steps.documents_needed: Medicare/Medicaid documentation, denial letters
steps.deadline: Varies by program
steps.notes: CLAIM provides free Medicare counseling. MO HealthNet Division handles managed care complaints.

steps.action: Escalate to MO AG Consumer Protection or CFPB (for financial products). AG can pursue pattern violations by insurers.
steps.documents_needed: All prior documentation, evidence of pattern if applicable
steps.deadline: No strict deadline — pattern threshold for AG action
steps.notes: AG can pursue insurers for pattern of unfair claim practices
